description: **Early exit, output writers, and signals.** `strictcli.ExitNow(code, message)` ends a command from anywhere in its call stack through the exit step: deferred functions run, the command exits `code`, and the message is printed as `error: <message>` (under `--json`, the last error diagnostic); `strictcli.Go(ctx, fn)` runs a goroutine whose `ExitNow` or panic is delivered to the handler, `App.Call` returns `*strictcli.ExitError`, and MCP answers `exit code <code>: <message>`. `ctx.Out(text)` writes the command's answer and is never hidden by `--quiet`; `PayloadRenderer(fn)` declares a human rendering of the payload; `ctx.Document()` writes an `OwnsStdout()` command's document. `App.Run` catches SIGINT and SIGTERM while the handler runs and closes `ctx.Done()`; when the handler returns, the command exits 130 or 143 with `error: canceled by signal <SIGNAL>`, and a second signal gets the default action.

**The `--json` document is `interface_version` 3, stdout is guarded under `--json`, and warnings and errors are prefixed.** The document carries an `output` member after `payload` (the text `ctx.Out` wrote plus captured child stdout, `null` when none); a child run through `Spawn` or `Run(Stream(true))` under `--json` no longer writes beside it. While a handler runs in machine mode, file descriptor 1 is redirected, and any byte written outside the framework (`fmt.Println`, `os.Stdout`, an unmanaged child) fails the run with exit 1 unless the code is already nonzero, plus the error diagnostic `stdout written outside the framework: <n> bytes: "<excerpt>"`. In human mode `ctx.Warn` prints `warning: <message>` and `ctx.Error` prints `error: <message>`.

**--lint-framework-use.** Every app reserves `--lint-framework-use`, which scans the program run from its module root (every strictcli main package and the module packages it imports, resolving import aliases) for process exits, direct stdout and stderr writes, argv access, environment reads, and `strictcli.ExitNow` inside a raw `go` func literal, and exits 1 listing each finding as `<path>:<line>: <rule>: <message>`.

Under `--json` the runtime guard now redirects stdout at the operating-system level on every Unix (including Solaris, illumos, and AIX) and on Windows, so a direct write to the standard output or a child started outside the effects handle is caught there too. The module now requires `golang.org/x/sys`.

A child started through `ctx.Effects().Spawn` that is still running when its handler ends is now killed (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after one second; at once on Windows) and fails the run: exit 1 unless the status is already nonzero, plus `error: child process <pid> was still running when the handler ended and was killed: <argv>`. The exit step no longer waits for such a child. Wait on every child you spawn, or end it with the new `Spawned.Kill()`; `Spawned.Signal(sig)` sends any signal.
`ExitError` gains `Payload`: what the command supplied through `ctx.Payload` before its early exit, nil when it supplied nothing.
